beats.narration: Begin by framing Course Structure Overview as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. The other thread is an independent project. Consider this worked case: A student might choose 'Machine Learning in Healthcare' for the survey thread and 'Developing a Low-Cost IoT Sensor Network' for the independent thread. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.
beats.title: Course Structure Overview
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Create an editable process diagram for Course Structure Overview with labeled inputs, decisions, state changes, and a checked output.

beats.narration: Now define Survey Paper Requirements precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Students will select, read and collectively discuss papers from conferences and journals in CS. Consider this worked case: Students will curate five recent ACM SIGCOMM papers on secure messaging protocols and synthesize their methodologies into a comparative analysis. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
beats.title: Survey Paper Requirements
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a flowchart starting with 'Select Papers', moving to 'Read & Annotate', then 'Collective Discussion', and ending with 'Draft Survey Paper' with clear arrows and concise labels.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Independent Project Workflow operates in a concrete sequence. Students will select a topic, lay out weekly goals, and meet with the instructor weekly. Consider this worked case: A student developing a natural language processing tool will submit a one-page weekly milestone document detailing progress, obstacles, and next steps. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
beats.title: Independent Project Workflow
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Render a horizontal timeline spanning the semester with ten weekly markers, each containing a placeholder for 'Weekly Goal' and 'Meeting Notes', emphasizing iterative progress.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Final Deliverables and make the decision criteria explicit. A final report and presentation will be required. Consider this worked case: The survey paper culminates in a 15-page manuscript with an abstract, while the independent project ends with a 10-page technical report and a 10-minute defense presentation. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
beats.title: Final Deliverables
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Create a two-column layout comparing the 'Survey Paper Final Report' and 'Independent Project Final Report', highlighting required sections like methodology, results, and limitations.

beats.narration: Apply Admission Requirements to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. Enrollment in this course requires permission from the department offering the course. Consider this worked case: Students must submit a proposal outlining their chosen research topics and a brief statement of how the course aligns with their degree requirements before registration opens. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
beats.title: Admission Requirements
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a checklist graphic with three items: 'Departmental Permission', 'Research Proposal Submission', and 'Academic Readiness Confirmation', each marked with a checkbox.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Ethical Computing Standards, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. They should respect privacy. Consider this worked case: When analyzing datasets for the independent project, students must anonymize participant information and explicitly state how data privacy was maintained. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
beats.title: Ethical Computing Standards
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Present a circular diagram with the ACM Code of Ethics principles radiating outward: 'Avoid Harm', 'Be Honest', 'Respect Privacy', 'Maintain High Quality', and 'Honor Confidentiality'.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Research Integrity Practices with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. Consider this worked case: Students will use reference managers to track citations, ensuring every methodological step and data source is properly attributed in the final report. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Research Integrity Practices
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a before-and-after comparison of a paragraph: the 'Before' version contains vague claims without citations, while the 'After' version includes precise citations and clearly separates observed evidence from author conclusions.

beats.narration: Use Methodological Rigor to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Consider this worked case: When documenting the independent project's algorithm, students will include pseudocode, parameter settings, and baseline comparisons to enable independent verification. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.
beats.title: Methodological Rigor
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a 'Research Integrity Checklist' with three boxes: 'Methods Described Clearly', 'Results Reported Accurately', and 'Limitations Disclosed', each with a brief explanatory note.

beats.narration: Connect Stakeholder & Impact Analysis to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations. Consider this worked case: Students will draft a brief stakeholder impact matrix for their independent project, mapping how their system might affect users, developers, and regulatory bodies. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
beats.title: Stakeholder & Impact Analysis
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Design a 2x2 matrix grid labeled 'Stakeholders' (rows) and 'Impact Dimensions' (columns: Benefits, Harms, Uncertainty, Obligations), with example cells filled for clarity.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Consider this worked case: A learner maps the inputs, constraints, and observable result for Practical Analysis Checklist, then checks each step against the stated claim. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Provide a printable one-page checklist template with checkboxes for 'Topic Selected', 'Weekly Goals Documented', 'Citations Verified', 'Ethical Review Completed', and 'Final Report & Presentation Ready', with space for student signature.

sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.excerpt: This course allows students to pursue two threads of research in computer science. One thread is the discovery and analysis of previous work in the field. Students will select, read and collectively discuss papers from conferences and journals in CS. A survey paper on a topic of the student's choice will be required. The other thread is an independent project. Students will select a topic, lay out weekly goals, and meet with the instructor weekly. A final report and presentation will be required. Enrollment in this course requires permission from the department offering the course. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 Typically Offered: Fall, Spring
sources.title: RIT CSCI-571 Honors Capstone Research catalog description

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.
sources.title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.
sources.title: ACM Publications Policies
